And it also would be extended far beyond that group, actually, to individuals who have, or even would be eligible for TPS, which is temporary protective status, and deferred enforced departure status, which is always intended as kind of a temporary opportunity for persons coming from other nations or torn nations, for instance, or nations dealing with a natural catastrophe. So essentially what it does is gives these individuals the opportunity to have immediate permanent status and an immediate special pathway to citizenship allows them to kind of jump ahead of all the folks that have been doing it right and have been waiting for their opportunities to come into America for many, many years. And so, initially, there might be some folks who could think, well, hey, we should do something about these dreamers, and I'm not altogether insensitive to that, but it cannot be done in a way that does not solve a larger immigration problem that we see unfolding at the border right now. There's definitely a crisis at the border that is not being addressed by House Democrats. The president is doing his best to address it. But he's got to have cooperation, frankly, from Congress, and he's not getting that. We've got a situation at our southern border where we have almost 150,000 people in the month of May alone that have been intercepted by Border Patrol. In the first seven months of this fiscal year, we have more than any previous year total since 2009. We've got unaccompanied minors coming across in record numbers. We have even people coming across from, we had this past a week, a group of about a thousand people in one particular group that came across together. So, unfortunately, we've got a larger immigration problem that has been created over a series of decades. And there's got to be a larger solution to it, which includes protection of our border integrity. And in my opinion, the bill that was passed does nothing to do that and address the crisis. And in fact, would only make it worse because it incentivizes people to get over here as quickly as they can so that then they can kind of jump ahead of the line in front of people that have been doing it right and follow the law. I think we have the right as a nation to determine what are the specific individuals in terms of their expertise and their skill and whatnot to come into the nation. I do think though that since they were brought here against, you know, they clearly were children when it happened. that they should have an opportunity to apply for citizenship and possibly have permanent status.
